skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest CT showing a combination of nodules and cysts to distinguish between cystic lung diseases.
steps: Assess the vertical distribution of abnormalities, specifically checking if the lung bases (costophrenic angles) are relatively spared compared to the upper and middle zones.
Examine the morphology of the cysts and nodules; look for bizarre, irregular, or confluent cyst shapes and thick-walled nodules that may cavitate.

Differentiate from Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM), which typically presents with uniform, round, thin-walled cysts and diffuse involvement including the bases, whereas the target diagnosis shows upper/mid-zone predominance with basal sparing.

skills.trigger: When identifying specific parenchymal patterns on high-resolution CT to support a diagnosis of histiocytic lung disease.
steps: Scan the lung windows for a reticulonodular pattern characterized by the coexistence of small centrilobular nodules and cystic spaces.
Verify the presence of 'bizarre' or stellate-shaped cysts rather than simple spherical lucencies.
Confirm the absence of significant fibrosis or honeycombing in the subpleural regions of the lower lobes to rule out idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
